# Performance and Architecture Changes in Halogen Changelog

## Version Timeline
**0.7.0** (earliest detailed): First GGUF support
**0.15.0** (latest): Default checkpoint updated to qwen38-flash-next-v2.hgn

## Kernel and Compute Changes

**0.12.0** – Sparse attention indexer optimization:
- "Decode at long context was paying for the indexer's block SELECT"
- Serial decode: "30.0 -> 35.2 tok/s at 262k and 18.9 -> 32.1 at 1M"
- With draft head: "43.5 -> 49.4 and 27.2 -> 41.7"
- "Prefill at 1M was paying twice for the same indexer"
- 1M prefill: "1,191 -> 994 s (877 -> 1,051 tok/s)"

**0.14.1** – Routed-expert prefill kernel:
- "Prefill uses a new routed-expert kernel"
- "Prefill numerics change at rounding level on prompts of 64 tokens or more"

**0.14.0** – Draft head improvements:
- Draft head: "proposes more tokens that the model accepts: 2.47 committed a round against 1.68"
- Speed gain: "52.3 tokens per second against 44.4 (+18%)" and "46.0 against 39.9 (+15%)"
- "On ten served prompt shapes that is 52.3 tokens per second against 44.4"

## Memory and Quantization

**0.11.6** – K-quant GGUF support:
- "K-quant file's perplexity and fixture agreement are its own"
- Performance: "0.020 nats better perplexity than UD-IQ4_XS"
- "about 3% slower serial decode"

# Technical Passages from halogen-flash-server Documentation

## Power and Thermal Specifications

"**about 85 W of sustained package power**, sampled from sysfs during a 32,768-token prefill alongside a 2,229 MHz median clock against the part's 2,900 MHz top state."

Context: This describes measurement conditions on the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, establishing the power envelope used for all performance benchmarks.

"with `iommu=pt` we measured the SoC drawing more power (122 to 127 W against 108 to 118) for lower shader clocks (2,357 to 2,409 MHz against 2,549 to 2,713 MHz)"

Context: Demonstrates how IOMMU settings affect power draw and clock frequencies, with detailed before-and-after measurements.

"**Match the power envelope before comparing decode numbers.** It is the condition most easily left out and it moves these rows: an independent tester running a 70 W-limited handheld measured 11 to 12 percent under both the serial and the drafted figure below"

Context: Emphasizes that power constraints significantly impact performance metrics and must be controlled when comparing results.

## Software Stack and Architecture

"ROCm 7.14.0, and **about 85 W of sustained package power**"

Context: Specifies the AMD ROCm version used in official measurements.

"Every kernel is written for this one GPU and this one model family. No general-purpose runtime, no portability layer, no fallback path."

Context: Describes the optimization strategy—custom kernels rather than abstracted backends.

"the engine's own per-request line, copied" and "the engine's own occupancy: the positions its pool holds in every region, busy and held"

Context: References internal engine metrics and monitoring capabilities.

## Quantization and Precision Details

"**Precision: 5.53 bpw**, measured from the checkpoint's own tensor table rather than quoted from a format name. That is across all 179.55B parameters, or 4.55 bpw across the trunk and experts with the FP8 n-gram lookup table set aside."

Context: Specifies bit-per-weight measurements with breakdown by tensor family.

"the experts and the rest of the model at 4 bits, the small mixing layers between them at 6 bits, and the draft head's projections at 8"

Context: Describes precision allocation across model components.

"int4" and "int8" references appear in schema/format discussions but are used as standard notation rather than novel technical claims.

## Container and Deployment

"podman run --rm -p 8731:8731 ... ghcr.io/peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server:0.15.0"

Context: Shows deployment via container image from GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io).

"The tag is pinned on purpose, and `:latest` exists too."

Context: Documents versioning strategy for the container image.

"On Docker rather than Podman, replace `--group-add keep-groups`"

Context: Discusses container runtime compatibility.

## Model Architecture Features

"DeltaNet layer" references appear throughout but are treated as model-specific architectural terms rather than novel claims about the technology.

"sparse-attention indexer: its block select ran serial in the context length on one compute unit at decode"

Context: Describes optimization of sparse attention mechanisms for decode performance.

"**The four 0.12.0 rows are served, through this image, at the 1M configuration**"

Context: References long-context configurations with specific memory/performance tradeoffs.

content.text:
Private list: nothing further. The fold-in is written, the claims are checked against fresh measurements, and no item depends on anything outstanding.

Both parts are done. The energy roofline is folded into KERNELS.md (decision 1 amended, a new roofline section, a G0b stage, G2 re-ordered so fewer-bytes-per-FLOP arms come before the prefetch, G7 reframed) and filed as research §0.7. On the halogen claims, I measured our side rather than guess.

**What the page actually is.** The repository is documentation plus a container image. GitHub classes it as Shell, it is 1 MB, and there is no kernel source anywhere in it. The license is a custom one. So the numbers can be reproduced by running their image, but the how cannot be read. The clearest technical statements are a 4.16-bit checkpoint (experts and trunk at 4 bits, mixing layers 6, draft head 8), a routed-expert prefill kernel, a sparse-attention indexer fix, and a draft head that commits 2.47 tokens a round. The 85 W figure is package power sampled from sysfs during a 32k prefill, at a 2229 MHz median clock.

**The claims against ours.** I ran our prefill and decode at 24 of 48 layers with the sampler, since the whole model does not fit beside the resting service.

| | theirs | ours | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefill, 8k prompt | 1,584 tok/s | 1,213 tok/s | 1.3x them |
| prefill, 128k to 131k | 1,517 tok/s | 1,011 to 1,022 tok/s | 1.5x them |
| prefill power | 85 W at 2229 MHz | 142 W at 2713 MHz | 2x the joules a token |
| serial decode, short context | 37.6 tok/s | 34.4 tok/s | within 10% |
| serial decode, deep | 34.1 at 32k | 31.5 at 128k | within 10% |
| decode power | 108 to 118 W (from their IOMMU note) | 91 W | about equal joules a token |
| speculative decode | 46 to 56 tok/s | parked at 0.95x | the gap |

So three findings. The decode claim is ordinary: their serial rate matches ours at similar energy, and the 56 figure is a draft head plus prompt lookup on coding-agent turns where half the tokens are copies, which is exactly the loop we parked. The prefill claim is the real one: 1.25 to 1.5x faster at a lower clock and 60% of the power, which is about twice our energy efficiency per token. That signature, faster at a lower clock, means fewer bytes moved per token through the memory system, not lower-power instructions. It points at G5 (4-bit weights straight into the matrix cores without the LDS round trip, where our MoE GEMM sits at 51%) and G6 (the streaming kernels between the GEMMs). Our own decode draws only 91 W, which confirms it is bytes-bound and the clock is not its problem.

One thing I did not do: run their image on this machine. It would settle whether the 85 W is their box's power cap or their kernels' appetite, but it means a 60 to 70 GB closed binary with GPU access on the deployed server, so that is your call.
